h1: The 6 Best PIR Motion Sensor Lights of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best PIR Motion Sensor Lights: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 PIR motion sensor lights scored on detection range, lumen output and mounting, from a 5500-lumen flood to a socket adapter.
summary: The ShineSeed 45W dual-head flood is the PIR light for outdoor coverage: 5500 lumens, a 180 degree sensor and an IP65 rating. For a porch or garage fixture you already own, the Torkase bulb is the simplest upgrade. Closets and pantries suit the slochi 1500-lumen ceiling light, and the Taigeguang socket adds motion sensing to a lamp you already have.
intro: A PIR sensor does not see motion, it sees heat that moves across its field of view. That is why a PIR light fires reliably on a person crossing the lens, and fires late or not at all when someone walks straight toward it. The sensor's lens angle and mounting height decide more about real performance than any lumen figure on the box.

We ranked six PIR lights on the Primea framework, covering a bulb, a socket adapter, two ceiling fixtures and an outdoor flood. Scoring weights detection range and angle first, then brightness, adjustability and the quality of the mounting spec, since a sensor mounted 3 feet too high or too low turns a good product into an unreliable one.

products.name: ShineSeed 45W 5500LM Dual-Head PIR Flood Light
products.verdict: Wide, bright and weatherproof: 5500 lumens, a 180 degree sensor and IP65 protection.
products.description:
Two adjustable heads put out 45W and 5500 lumens at 5000K, with a 180 degree PIR sensor and an IP65 waterproof rating. Three daily modes plus a test mode let you set when it turns on, which shortens the setup that most flood lights make painful.

It tops the list because the 180 degree field covers a driveway or yard edge that a bulb sensor cannot reach. The Torkase bulb is easier to install but throws a fraction of the light, and the indoor ceiling lights are not weatherproof at all.

Buy it for driveways, garages and yard perimeters. The caveat is that 5000K daylight white is harsh near bedroom windows, and the $25 to $50 price is the highest of the six.
products.idealFor: Driveways, garages and yard perimeters that need wide, weatherproof coverage.
products.skipIf: You want a warm light near bedroom windows.

products.name: Torkase E26 PIR Motion Sensor Light Bulb
products.verdict: A 1100-lumen, 100W-equivalent bulb that adds motion sensing to any E26 fixture.
products.description:
Brightness is 1100 lumens, equal to a 100W bulb, with a detection range of 8 to 16 feet, an E26 base and dusk-to-dawn activation. A built-in security glow keeps a low light on between detections.

It ranks second because installation takes seconds and the output is strong for a screw-in. It falls behind the ShineSeed on coverage, since a bulb senses in the direction it points, and the sensor looks out from the socket instead of aiming at the approach path.

Best for porches, garages and entries with an existing fixture. The caveat is placement: a bulb inside an enclosed or sideways fixture can lose sensing range.
products.idealFor: Porches, garages and entries where bright light is wanted the instant someone arrives.
products.skipIf: Your fixture is enclosed or points sideways.

products.name: slochi 15W Hardwired PIR Closet Ceiling Light
products.verdict: A 7 inch, 1500-lumen flush ceiling light with three sensor modes and three hold times.
products.description:
Output is 15W and 1500 lumens in a 7 inch flush-mount disc, with 120 degree detection at 3 to 4 meters and a mounting height of 2 to 3 meters. Three sensor modes and three hold times, plus color temperatures of 3000K, 4000K or 6500K, give plenty of tuning.

It ranks third because the fixture is hardwired and indoor only. Its 1500 lumens are more than the 800-lumen GREENIC bulb provides, and the three hold times beat the ECOELER's single countdown for pantries and closets.

Buy it for closets, pantries and utility rooms. The caveat is that a flush ceiling mount needs a junction box, which puts it beyond a quick plug-in swap.
cons: 120 degree field is narrower than a flood
products.idealFor: Pantries, closets and small utility rooms that need a lot of ceiling light.
products.skipIf: You want a no-wiring plug-in solution.

products.name: GREENIC 9W A19 PIR Motion Sensor Light Bulb
products.verdict: An 800-lumen, 5000K A19 bulb with a clearly published mounting height of 6.8 to 8 feet.
products.description:
Nine watts produce 800 lumens, a 60W equivalent, at 5000K daylight. Detection reaches 10 to 13 feet from a recommended mounting height of 6.8 to 8 feet, and a dusk-to-dawn photocell holds it off in daylight.

It ranks fourth because it is dimmer and has a shorter range than the Torkase, yet the published mounting height is the most useful number in the whole group. A bulb installed outside that height range loses reliability, and few listings state it.

Use it for stoops, laundry rooms and carports with ceilings around 7 feet. The caveat is the 800-lumen ceiling, which is modest for a large outdoor space.
products.idealFor: Stoops, laundry rooms and carports where a moderate daylight bulb is enough.
products.skipIf: You need a high-ceiling or long-range sensor.

products.name: ECOELER 16W PIR Motion Sensor Ceiling Light
products.verdict: A 16W flush light with selectable 3000K, 4000K and 5000K plus an adjustable delay.
products.description:
The ECOELER is a flush-mount occupancy light drawing 16W, with three selectable color temperatures (3000K, 4000K and 5000K), an adjustable time delay with a countdown, and dusk-to-dawn sensing built in.

It sits fifth because it publishes no lumen count or detection range, which makes it hard to compare with the slochi's 1500 lumens and 3 to 4 meter range. The selectable color temperature is a real plus for a hallway or utility room where you want warm light at night.

Buy it for hallways, closets and laundry rooms. The caveat is the missing performance numbers, so confirm size and coverage before you commit.
products.idealFor: Closets, hallways and utility rooms that need a tunable ceiling light with a timer.
products.skipIf: You compare fixtures strictly by lumens and range.

products.name: Taigeguang E26/E27 PIR Motion Sensor Light Socket
products.verdict: An indoor-only screw-in adapter that turns any bulb into a motion-sensing one.
products.description:
This is not a light but a socket: it screws into an E26 or E27 lamp holder and accepts your own bulb. A time button and a second-adjustment control tune the hold time, and it detects human infrared energy, then switches the light on and off.

It ranks last because the brightness depends entirely on your bulb and no detection range is published. Its virtue is flexibility: you can reuse a warm bulb you already like, which none of the other five allow.

Use it in closets or hallway lamp holders. The caveat is that it is indoor only, and a bulky adapter can protrude beyond a shallow shade.
products.idealFor: Indoor lamp holders where you want to reuse your own bulb and add motion control.
products.skipIf: You need outdoor use or a published detection range.

methodology.title: Detection range and angle
methodology.description: Published distance and field of view, since they decide how early the light fires on an approach.

methodology.title: Brightness and color
methodology.description: Lumen output and color temperature relative to the intended space.

methodology.title: Adjustability
methodology.description: Hold-time, sensor mode and daylight lockout controls.

methodology.title: Mounting and weather rating
methodology.description: Published mounting heights, installation effort and IP rating for outdoor use.

methodology.title: Spec transparency and value
methodology.description: Whether the listing states range and lumens, and price bucket against that.

whatMatters.detail: PIR senses moving heat, so wide angles catch crossing movement better than head-on approach. The ShineSeed offers 180 degrees, the slochi 120 degrees at 3 to 4 meters. Look for both a distance and an angle on the listing, and favor a wide field for outdoor use.

A PIR lens is tuned for a specific height. The GREENIC states 6.8 to 8 feet and the slochi 2 to 3 meters. Mount outside the range and sensitivity drops. Match the stated height to your porch ceiling or soffit before buying, because it cannot be fixed afterward.

Lumens measure output and color temperature sets the mood. The ShineSeed's 5500 lumens at 5000K cut through a yard, while the ECOELER's 3000K setting suits a hallway. Pick output for the space and tone for the people who walk through it at night.

Hold time is how long the light stays on after motion stops, and the lockout keeps it off in daylight. The slochi offers three hold times, the Torkase and GREENIC use dusk-to-dawn sensors. A short hold wastes energy less, a long one suits closets and stairs.

Outdoor fixtures need an IP rating. The ShineSeed carries IP65, meaning dust tight and protected from water jets. The ceiling lights and the Taigeguang socket are indoor only. An enclosed outdoor fixture also traps heat, which shortens bulb life, so check the bulb's listed use.

faq.q: Will the Torkase bulb work in an enclosed fixture?
faq.a: It may, but sensing range suffers. A sealed glass globe blocks infrared from reaching the sensor and traps heat. Use the Torkase in an open fixture, and choose the ShineSeed flood if you only have a covered outdoor box.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with PIR lights?
faq.a: Mounting outside the stated height. The GREENIC specifies 6.8 to 8 feet and the slochi 2 to 3 meters. A sensor too high or too low misses movement. Measure your ceiling or soffit first, then pick the model that matches.

faq.q: Is the ShineSeed worth it over a bulb?
faq.a: For wide outdoor areas, yes. Its 180 degree sensor and 5500 lumens cover a driveway that the Torkase, with 1100 lumens and 8 to 16 feet of range, cannot. For a small porch, the Torkase bulb is simpler and cheaper.

faq.q: How do I set up the ShineSeed?
faq.a: Mount it, then use the test mode to walk through the sensing zone and adjust the head angles. Three daily modes set whether it runs all night or only after dark. Aim the sensor across the approach, not straight at it.

Wipe the sensor lens and fixture occasionally, because dust and spider webs trigger false alarms. The outdoor ShineSeed can be hosed lightly given its IP65 rating. Indoor models like the slochi should only be wiped with a dry cloth.

faq.q: Can the Taigeguang socket run an LED bulb?
faq.a: It is designed to switch your own bulb, but check wattage and dimmer compatibility on the listing. It detects human infrared energy and offers adjustable hold times, so a low-wattage LED is typically fine for a closet lamp.

finalTake: The ShineSeed 45W 5500LM Dual-Head PIR Flood Light is the best PIR light for anyone who needs real outdoor coverage, while the Torkase bulb is the quick upgrade for an existing fixture. Choose the slochi for closets and pantries, and remember to check mounting height before you buy. PIR performance depends on where the sensor sits, not just the lumen number.
